answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can require each participant to lock a copper-scale deposit that is forfeited on proven fraud. Think of a harbor charging every arriving ship a refundable berthing fee: one honest captain pays once and docks freely, while an attacker flooding the harbor with a hundred fake vessels pays the fee a hundred times. No fable of decentralization survives when identity costs nothing; the bond turns one-agent-one-voice from a wish into arithmetic, because spawning the Nth sybil costs exactly as much as the first.
